decision: v5 and v6: viewer queue = outstanding / bytes the viewer link retired in the last 250 ms - viewer MinRtt
why: SendBufferingEnabled is off, so outstanding includes one RTT in flight; the denominator must be the link's rate, not the sharer's, or the sharer's own skipping inflates it
result: built clean; r3 started with v5 v6

decision: wrote the premise down: a rate-normalised viewer queue falls when the sharer sends less, so refusals self-limit; tested it with per-second server and sharer logs on one v5 E run
why: two fixes sharing one premise failed the same way, so test the belief before a third fix
result: premise false: every refusal was viewer-side while sampled server queue read 0; an in-flight frame over an app-limited rate reads as 150-550 ms, and refusals starve the reports that would clear them (report age up to 555 ms)

decision: v7 and v8: viewer queue = age of the oldest unacknowledged byte minus MinRtt, from per-viewer (cumulative bytes, time) marks; sharer drains a reported queue by its age
why: removes the rate from the signal instead of compensating for it, and stops stale reports holding refusals
result: single E run: 50.5 fps, 2 freezes, 69% link use, p95 157 ms (was 6 fps, 54 freezes); r4 started for v7 v8

decision: r4: v7 cut freezes to 0-2 per run (off had 14-44) with 71-96% link use; v8's cap throttled E to 37% of the link; v7-B and v8-A failed in the harness (clients hung on quit, next server could not start)
why: treat the two harness failures as environment until a rerun says otherwise; the user's own Parties client was running and shares the GPU
result: v7 kept as base, v8 dropped

decision: traced a residual v7 freeze: bottleneck queue reached its 100 ms drop-tail, packets dropped, retransmits tripped the gate; v7 only refuses frames at 120 ms and slows AIMD at 80 ms
